title: Who actually operates Amazon Air aircraft? The airlines behind Amazon's cargo fleet
description:
Amazon Air is an air freight service that moves packages between fulfilment centres and sorting hubs.
A number of companies operate the cargo aircraft for Amazon: Air Transport International One of the biggest operators of the Amazon Air network is Air Transport International (ATI).
It is part of the Air Transport Services Group (ATSG) and previously provided aircraft and crew to Amazon before Amazon Air launched.
ABX Air ABX Air is another Amazon Air carrier partner and is also part of ATSG.
Amazon’s current Amazon Air Cargo website lists ABX among its direct air carrier partners.
text:
An Amazon-branded cargo jet operated by 21 Air recently made headlines following a runway overrun at Miami International Airport. The incident on 6 September remains under investigation.

Yet it highlights a little-known aspect of Amazon’s air cargo network: although Amazon has access to a fleet of more than 100 aircraft, it doesn’t actually operate the flights.

Instead the aircraft are flown by a network of specialist cargo carriers that provide the pilots, maintenance, and the regulatory approvals needed to conduct the flights.

What is Amazon Air?

Amazon Air is an air freight service that moves packages between fulfilment centres and sorting hubs.

Amazon launched the operation in the US in 2016 on wet leases. Its first aircraft, a Boeing 767 known as Amazon One, took to the skies that year and the operation expanded rapidly.

By December 2018, 40 aircraft were flying in and out of more than 20 US airports, with Boeing 737 freighters added for shorter routes, and Boeing 767s for higher-capacity operations.

Amazon expanded internationally and by 2022, its global network had grown to over 100 aircraft. By 2024, Amazon Air was serving more than 70 destinations worldwide.

Today, Amazon Air Cargo says its network has more than 100 aircraft and 250 daily flights, operated by carrier partners. On its website it states, “Amazon is not an air carrier: we provide ACAR Services by contracting with air carriers that operate the aircraft.”

Who flies Amazon aircraft?

A number of companies operate the cargo aircraft for Amazon:

Air Transport International

One of the biggest operators of the Amazon Air network is Air Transport International (ATI). It is part of the Air Transport Services Group (ATSG) and previously provided aircraft and crew to Amazon before Amazon Air launched.

According to ATSG’s 2024 SEC filing, at the end of 2024 ATSG was leasing 30 Boeing 767 freighters to Amazon and operating 21 Boeing 767s provided by Amazon.

ABX Air

ABX Air is another Amazon Air carrier partner and is also part of ATSG. Amazon’s current Amazon Air Cargo website lists ABX among its direct air carrier partners.

Sun Country Airlines

Another major Amazon Air operator is Sun Country Airlines. The Minneapolis-based passenger and cargo airline has operated Amazon cargo flights since 2020.

On its website, Sun County Airlines says its cargo operation flies 20 Amazon-owned freighters.

21 Air

Fleet data from industry experts Cirium shows 21 Air operating eight aircraft for Amazon.

The operator has been in the headlines following the runway overrun at Miami Airport on 6 September. The Amazon Air cargo jet involved was operated by 21 Air.

The National Transportation Safety Board is currently investigating the incident and no cause has been given.

Hawaiian Airlines

Amazon also uses Hawaiian Airlines to operate its largest freighters: Airbus A330-300 converted freighters.

Amazon announced the deal in 2022, saying Hawaiian would maintain and operate an initial fleet of 10 aircraft on Amazon’s behalf.

Despite Hawaiian’s acquisition by Alaska Air Group, the operation continues under Hawaiian.

ASL Airlines Ireland

In Europe, Amazon uses ASL Airlines Ireland. This is part of ASL Aviation Holdings.

ASL says it operates freight aircraft for companies and online retailers including Amazon, DHL and FedEx.

QuikJet

In India, Amazon Air operates through QuikJet Airlines. The Indian cargo carrier is part of the ASL Aviation group.

Amazon launched its dedicated air cargo operation in India in 2023.

Cargojet

Amazon has used Canada’s Cargojet to operate Amazon-owned Boeing 767 freighters.

How many aircraft does Amazon Air have?

Amazon Air says its network includes more than 100 aircraft globally.

Does Amazon own any of the aircraft?

In January 2021, Amazon announced its first purchase of aircraft, buying 11 Boeing 767-300s from Delta Air Lines and WestJet.

It also leases a significant number of aircraft.

Why doesn’t Amazon operate its own cargo jets?

Running an airline involves a lot more than just owning aircraft. It requires pilots, maintenance teams and extensive operational infrastructure.

Instead of building and managing all that itself, Amazon contracts specialist airlines that already have those systems, personnel and regulatory approvals in place.

Who is responsible for flight safety?

The flight preparation and operational safety decisions are made by the air carrier, rather than Amazon.

On its website, Amazon says, “The air carrier’s pilot-in-command has full authority over preparation and acceptance of cargo for transport on the aircraft and all other aspects of flight safety.”

Air carriers must follow FAA rules, including preflight planning.

This means when an Amazon-branded aircraft is involved in an incident, investigations are typically conducted with the airline operating the flight, which holds the air operator certificate and conducts the flight operations.

title: Palm Oil Substitute Made From Greenhouse Gas Emissions - Intelligent Living
description:
Rainforest clearance for oil palm plantations has destroyed critical habitats and displaced endangered wildlife like orangutans and Sumatran rhinos.
Researchers have turned industrial greenhouse gases into a sustainable palm oil substitute.
The Palm Oil Paradox: A Global Need Versus Environmental Cost The world’s reliance on vegetable oils creates a dilemma for manufacturers and consumers alike.
Replacing palm oil with other crop oils would require far more agricultural land, driving even more deforestation and habitat destruction.
Programs like the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil set ecological standards, but tracing every drop through global supply chains remains difficult.
text:
For decades, palm oil has been a staple of modern manufacturing. It appears in roughly half of all packaged products sold in supermarkets today. You will find it in baked goods, chocolates, margarine, laundry detergents, and luxury cosmetics. Manufacturers prize it for its smooth texture, long shelf life, and versatility.

But its environmental cost is well documented. Rainforest clearance for oil palm plantations has destroyed critical habitats and displaced endangered wildlife like orangutans and Sumatran rhinos. Draining and burning ancient peatlands also release large stores of carbon dioxide back into the atmosphere.

Now, a scientific collaboration has found a radical way forward. Researchers have turned industrial greenhouse gases into a sustainable palm oil substitute. By capturing factory emissions before they reach the atmosphere, they are turning a global pollutant into a useful resource. The process needs no farmland at all, pointing to a future where everyday goods are made from the very gases driving climate change.

The Palm Oil Paradox: A Global Need Versus Environmental Cost

The world’s reliance on vegetable oils creates a dilemma for manufacturers and consumers alike. Palm oil is an exceptionally efficient crop. It yields between three and four tons of oil per hectare each year, roughly four to ten times more than soybean, sunflower, or coconut oil.

That efficiency creates a paradox. Replacing palm oil with other crop oils would require far more agricultural land, driving even more deforestation and habitat destruction.

Certified sustainable sourcing has struggled to keep pace with soaring demand. Programs like the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil set ecological standards, but tracing every drop through global supply chains remains difficult. There is simply not enough certified oil to supply the cosmetics, food, and biofuel sectors, where crop-based biofuel demand has already pressured tropical forests.

This leaves industries with no easy agricultural way out. Innovators are looking beyond farming altogether, seeking ways to make fats without planting a single seed. One earlier effort even replaced palm oil with coffee grounds recovered from cafe waste streams. A workable palm oil substitute is no longer a luxury. It is a necessity for global climate targets.

A Two-Stage Bioprocess: From Industrial Exhaust to Camembert Yeasts

The breakthrough rests on a clever, two-stage fermentation process. It was developed by the Fraunhofer Institute for Interfacial Engineering and Biotechnology (IGB) in Straubing, Germany, with the US carbon recycling firm LanzaTech and the Swiss cosmetics maker Mibelle Group. The method needs neither fertile soil nor farming.

Stage 1: Gas Fermentation Turns Emissions Into Ethanol

LanzaTech uses specialized bacteria to turn carbon dioxide- and carbon monoxide-rich industrial exhaust gases into ethanol. At commercial sites such as steel mills, continuous bioreactors capture the gases billowing from the flues. The process resembles brewing beer, except captured greenhouse gases replace grain as the raw material. The bacteria feed on the emissions and produce pure ethanol.

Stage 2: Cheese Yeasts Turn Ethanol Into Fat

Fraunhofer’s oil yeasts then ferment that ethanol into a rich, palm oil-like fat blend. These yeasts are oleaginous, meaning they naturally store high amounts of fat inside their cells. Both stages rely only on naturally occurring, non-genetically modified microorganisms. The yeasts Fraunhofer uses are naturally found on cheeses like Camembert. Fed with ethanol, they convert the alcohol into a thick biological fat that closely mirrors the chemical profile of tropical oils.

This approach echoes other advances in carbon capture, such as work on CO2-consuming bacteria that turn industrial waste into useful chemical building blocks. In each case, heavy industry’s waste becomes a high-value commodity.

Cosmetics Validation: Laboratory Success to Skin Care Trials

Making an alternative fat is only half the battle. It must also meet strict cosmetic standards. The beauty industry needs ingredients with specific melting points, stability, and skin feel. Above all, manufacturers want a drop-in replacement that slots into existing formulas without a redesign. After successful trials at Fraunhofer IGB, the fat blend went through application testing at Mibelle Laboratories to confirm it met these criteria.

The results confirmed a versatile, high-quality, 100% palm oil-free fat with strong skin-care properties. Because it is natural and biologically derived, it blends easily into lotions, creams, and other personal care items without the synthetic feel of petroleum-based alternatives. Industry leaders see major supply-chain potential. Peter Müller, CEO of the Mibelle Group, noted that “this innovation is the result of our long-standing partnership with LanzaTech and a milestone for the cosmetics industry.”

Susanne Heldmaier, Head of Research and Technical Innovation at the Mibelle Group, added, “Following successful research in the laboratory, we have now been able to start developing the pilot process… This will enable us to develop cosmetic products that not only protect our skin but also contribute to protecting the environment.” The tests show this palm oil substitute can compete on performance, paving the way for everyday products that are genuinely free from tropical deforestation.

Twice as Sustainable: Keeping Carbon in the Loop

This palm oil alternative earns its environmental credentials through a circular lifecycle. Conventional crop farming runs on a linear model that constantly demands fresh land and water. Project lead Vanessa Wegat from Fraunhofer IGB puts it simply: using climate-harmful emissions as raw material makes the finished product “twice as sustainable.”

The dual benefit is easy to see. First, the process avoids rainforest clearing because no arable land is needed to grow the Camembert yeasts. There is no fertilizer runoff, no pesticide use, and no habitat destruction.

Second, it uses raw industrial emissions directly, keeping greenhouse gases out of the atmosphere. The approach fits a broader wave of companies converting CO2 emissions into everyday products, from laundry detergent made from carbon emissions to advanced materials like polypropylene made from captured waste CO2. The result is a functional palm oil substitute that acts as a carbon sink while it is being made.

Beyond Cosmetics: Opening a New Route for Sustainable Aviation Fuel

Cosmetics offer an immediate, high-margin market that can fund further development. But the implications reach far beyond beauty products. Aviation, in particular, is desperate for low-carbon fuels. LanzaTech says the breakthrough could open a new route to the HEFA (Hydroprocessed Esters and Fatty Acids) pathway for sustainable aviation fuel, commonly called SAF.

Conventional SAF leans on limited supplies of used cooking oil, animal fats, or dedicated oil crops that compete with food production, though researchers have also pursued other routes from CO2 to green fuel. Collecting waste oils is logistically complex and capped by local supply. Turning crops into jet fuel triggers the same land-use controversies as tropical farming.

By making fatty acids straight from captured industrial gases, fuel developers could gain a huge, scalable feedstock that bypasses land-use conflicts and supply bottlenecks. The route works much like the Alcohol-to-Jet concept, but it uses the biological fats produced by the yeasts. Continuous bioreactors could supply the sheer volume of sustainable raw material needed to decarbonize commercial flight.

Scale-Up at Leuna: Preparing for Kilogram-Scale Pilot Production

Moving from a lab beaker to commercial reality takes serious engineering. Making a palm oil substitute in a petri dish is a triumph; supplying global manufacturers requires industrial output. The project has therefore moved to kilogram-scale pilot production, scaled up step-by-step at the Fraunhofer Center for Chemical-Biotechnological Processes (CBP) in Leuna, a branch of Fraunhofer IGB.

The Leuna facility is renowned for scaling up biochemical engineering processes. At pilot scale, engineers must solve three core challenges before commercial production can begin:

Optimizing mass transfer so yeast cultures receive a steady, uniform supply of ethanol as the bioreactors grow from liters to cubic meters.

Managing the heat generated by fermentation in large vats, since yeast productivity drops sharply if temperatures drift.

Maintaining continuous culture health over long production runs, keeping the non-GMO yeasts lipid-rich batch after batch.

The scaling economics are highly promising because the feedstock, primarily carbon waste, is incredibly cheap and abundant.

The joint announcement, detailed in their September 2025 press release, began an intensive scaling phase. As the technology matures, production costs should fall, letting the synthetic fat compete on price with cheap tropical oils. Fraunhofer’s 2026 research feature continues to highlight how greenhouse gases yield a palm oil alternative that meets industrial demand without ecological compromise. The path from pilot plants to commercial refineries should accelerate as global rules for sustainable ingredients tighten.

Comparing Sustainable Alternatives

To understand how this emissions-to-fat technology stacks up against traditional options, researchers and industry analysts look at several key metrics:

Feedstock / Method Land Use Deforestation Risk Scalability Regulatory Path Conventional Palm Oil High (Agricultural) High Limited by arable land Established Alternative Vegetable Oils Very High Moderate to High Constrained by crop yields Established Emissions-to-Fat Fermentation Negligible (Industrial footprint) None High (tied to industrial output) Emerging / Pilot phase

Conclusion: A New Chapter for Circular Manufacturing

Making a palm oil substitute from greenhouse gases marks a major leap for green chemistry. By combining industrial carbon capture with natural microbial fermentation, scientists show that we do not have to choose between useful products and environmental protection. LanzaTech’s gas-to-ethanol expertise and Fraunhofer’s yeast conversion together provide a blueprint for the future.

As pilot production scales up in Leuna, this technology points to a future where cosmetics, household items, and clean aviation fuels are made from yesterday’s pollution. Closing the carbon loop would ease the pressure on tropical rainforests. Turning waste into a global commodity shows that human ingenuity can solve the ecological crises it created. Manufacturers may soon have a true, drop-in alternative that protects biodiversity, captures carbon, and delivers quality to consumers worldwide.

title: Southwest leads new push for low-cost airline lounges - Aerospace Global News
description:
Airport lounges have long been associated with first class, business class and the world’s premier full-service airlines.
Southwest lounges will be closely tied to Chase Southwest is developing the lounges in partnership with Chase.
A new premium Southwest Rapid Rewards credit card issued by Chase will launch in 2027 and include access to the lounge network.
Southwest has not yet disclosed the card’s annual fee, guest policy or whether other passengers will be able to buy lounge access.
IndiGo ties lounge access to its loyalty programme and co-branded cards, while AirAsia X bundles third‑party lounge access with its premium onboard product.
text:
Airport lounges have long been associated with first class, business class and the world’s premier full-service airlines. But some low-cost carriers have included lounges in their passenger experience, despite their lean operating models.

Southwest Airlines is the latest—and one of the most significant—examples.

The US carrier has announced its first airport lounge network, with initial locations at Austin-Bergstrom International Airport (AUS), Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport (BWI), Daniel K. Inouye International Airport in Honolulu (HNL) and Nashville International Airport (BNA).

Construction has already begun, with the first lounges expected to open from late 2027. Southwest says at least seven more locations will follow over the next several years.

The move is another striking departure from the traditional low-cost model the airline first perfected, and so many others followed over the decades. Southwest has recently left its long-successful model behind, introducing assigned seating, extra-legroom seats and baggage charges.

But Southwest is not alone. A number of low-cost airlines see premium airport services as another service element passengers may be willing to pay for—either directly, through ancillaries, through airline loyalty programmes or by signing up for revenue-generating airline credit cards.

Southwest lounges will be closely tied to Chase

Southwest is developing the lounges in partnership with Chase. A new premium Southwest Rapid Rewards credit card issued by Chase will launch in 2027 and include access to the lounge network. Southwest has not yet disclosed the card’s annual fee, guest policy or whether other passengers will be able to buy lounge access.

Chase operates its own expanding Sapphire Reserve Lounge Network. However, none of the first four airports Southwest has announced as lounge locations currently has a Chase Sapphire Lounge.

Chase currently lists Sapphire lounges at Boston, Dallas/Fort Worth, New York JFK, Las Vegas, New York LaGuardia, Philadelphia, Phoenix and San Diego, with Los Angeles coming soon. Its wider card benefits also include Priority Pass lounges and selected Air Canada Maple Leaf Lounges.

Southwest says its new lounges will combine its own hospitality with the “success of the Chase Sapphire Reserve Lounge Network,” including sophisticated design, locally inspired food and amenities similar to those found in Chase lounges today.

Neither Southwest nor Chase has yet said who will own and operate the facilities. For now, the four new facilities appear to be a distinct Southwest-branded lounge network developed with Chase rather than new Chase Sapphire Lounges.

Lounges require significant investment in real estate and service. Southwest could recover that investment through Chase card revenue and possibly by selling lounge passes as ancillaries.

JetBlue has already moved into the lounge business

Southwest is not the first US airline with low-cost roots to make the move. JetBlue opened its first BlueHouse lounge at New York JFK Terminal 5 in December 2025. The 9,000-square-foot, two-level facility includes food and drinks, high-speed WiFi, charging points, quiet areas and a game room.

Its second BlueHouse opened at Boston Logan Terminal C on 27 August 2026.

Eligible Mint passengers get complimentary access, as do top-tier Mosaic loyalty programme members and qualifying JetBlue credit card holders. JetBlue also sells limited access to some other eligible passengers.

The lounges encourage bookings of JetBlue’s Mint premium cabin product, sign-ups for the TrueBlue loyalty programme, and credit card business, while also generating ancillary revenue through access passes.

easyJet finds lounge partner at Gatwick

In 2021, easyJet opened The Gateway at London Gatwick’s North Terminal. Rather than build and operate a proprietary lounge, easyJet partnered with No1 Lounges to run the facility.

The Gateway offered hot and cold food, drinks, WiFi, charging facilities, work areas, a TV den and games room.

The airline closed the easyJet Gateway Lounge over two years ago, and returned the property to No 1 Lounges. It now offers Inclusive Plus fare paying passengers access to My Lounge at Gatwick’s North Terminal, which is a separate No 1 Lounges property.

The airline has partnered with lounge operators to offer their facilities at other airports as a benefit for its higher-fare-paying passengers.

easyJet’s Inclusive Plus fare offers up to three hours of lounge stays at select locations.

Birmingham Airport (BHX) – No1 Lounge

Bristol Airport (BRS) – Escape Lounge

Edinburgh Airport (EDI) – Escape Lounge

Jersey Airport (JER) – No1 Lounge

London Gatwick Airport (LGW) – My Lounge North Terminal

Luton Airport (LTN) – My Lounge

Manchester Airport (MAN) – Escape Lounge Terminal 2

Stansted Airport (STN) – Escape Lounge

In Milan, easyJet grants access up to two hours before flight boarding time:

Milan Malpensa Airport (MXP) – Alda Merini Lounge, T2

Milan Linate Airport (LIN) – Leonardo Exclusive Lounge

The airline also sells lounge access as an ancillary product.

Norwegian and Scoot choose asset-light alternative

Building a lounge is not the only way for a low-cost carrier to sell passengers a more premium airport experience.

Norwegian has adopted an especially asset-light model through its Norwegian Reward partnership with Lounge Pass.

Norwegian Reward members can pre-book access to more than 800 independent airport lounges at more than 250 airports worldwide. The airline currently advertises access from £14 and awards members CashPoints worth 8% of the lounge booking.

It gives Norwegian an attractive lounge offer for passengers, covering a large geographical area, without having to build, staff or operate a single lounge.

Singapore-based Scoot has also used third-party lounges rather than investing in its own facilities. It previously sold a product called Scoot-in-Style at Singapore Changi, which bundled priority check-in and boarding with access to the SATS Premier Lounge. Scoot treated the lounge much like other optional airport services. The airline later discontinued the ancillary product and now directs passengers to buy their own access passes to run terminal lounges independently.

Lounge access as an ancillary service is the easiest way to integrate lounges into the low-cost model. Airlines do not need to own or manage premium ground infrastructure. Instead, they can connect passengers to existing lounge operators and earn loyalty, ancillary revenue or both.

IndiGo links lounges to fares, loyalty and credit cards

IndiGo applies a variation on the easyJet model, with a Southwest spin. Like easyJet, India’s largest airline provides premium airport services delivered by partners rather than building a large proprietary lounge network. Like Southwest, IndiGo’s lounge access supports its loyalty programme and branded credit card.

Its BluChip loyalty programme has, for example, partnered with AirportZo, allowing members to earn five IndiGo BluChips for every ₹100 spent on services including airport lounges, meet-and-greet and porter services.

IndiGo is also connecting lounge access with its expanding co-branded credit card business.

The premium IndiGo SBI credit card currently includes up to eight domestic and six international lounge visits annually, subject to its terms and spending requirements. Its premium Axis Bank card offers eight domestic and two international visits annually.

flynas combines its own lounges with a partner network

Saudi Arabian low-cost carrier flynas has gone considerably further. Unlike Norwegian or IndiGo, flynas has put its own name on airport lounges while also using partnerships to extend lounge benefits much further across its network.

A flynas-branded lounge is available at Jeddah’s King Abdulaziz International Airport and Dammam’s King Fahd International Airport.

The airline has also developed lounge access as a loyalty benefit. In 2024, flynas signed an agreement with Saudi lounge operator Hayyak, giving Prime members of its nasmiles loyalty programme complimentary access to 18 Hayyak lounges around the country when travelling with flynas. Other flynas passengers could purchase access through the airline’s website or app.

At the time, flynas said the Hayyak partnership complemented three flynas lounges at Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam. Its current lounge listings show how the model has evolved, with Hayyak now listed at Riyadh while Jeddah and Dammam retain flynas-branded facilities.

Prime nasmiles members continue to receive complimentary Hayyak lounge access when flying with flynas, subject to the programme’s conditions.

The result is effectively a hybrid lounge strategy: invest in branded facilities at key hub airports while using a specialist lounge operator to provide a much broader lounge network.

For a low-cost airline, that offers many of the advantages of a traditional global airline lounge network without requiring the carrier to build lounges at multiple destinations.

AirAsia X includes lounges with its premium seats

AirAsia X provides another example of a low-cost carrier using someone else’s lounge infrastructure to strengthen its most expensive onboard product.

The long-haul low-cost airline includes three hours of complimentary Plaza Premium Lounge access with its Premium Flatbed product at participating departure airports.

AirAsia X can offer one of the traditional benefits of international Business Class—a pre-flight lounge—without operating the facilities itself.

Air Arabia sells lounge access as another extra

Air Arabia follows a similarly asset-light approach. Like Norwegian, the Middle Eastern low-cost airline offers airport lounge access as an additional airport service passengers can add to their journeys, alongside products such as fast track and meet-and-assist.

This turns the lounge into another optional ancillary: passengers who value it can pay for it, while customers seeking the lowest possible fare can opt out.

flydubai takes a hybrid model approach to lounges

flydubai sits towards the premium end of the low-cost spectrum. Like JetBlue, it is closer to a hybrid carrier model than a traditional low-cost model. It opened its own dedicated Business Class Lounge at Dubai International Terminal 2 in December 2024.

Passengers travelling from Terminal 3 can instead use Emirates’ Business Class Lounge, while flydubai also provides access to partner lounges at numerous overseas destinations.

Lounges can make sense for low-cost airlines

JetBlue and flydubai invest in their own lounges. easyJet has branded a lounge built by a specialist company. flynas blends branded lounges with a broader partner network. Norwegian and Scoot use an asset-light approach, connecting passengers to independent lounge operators. IndiGo ties lounge access to its loyalty programme and co-branded cards, while AirAsia X bundles third‑party lounge access with its premium onboard product.

These strategies let low-cost airlines target passengers willing to spend more while keeping travel affordable for everyone else.

A lounge can create another paid ancillary, strengthen a premium fare bundle, reward high-value frequent flyers and make a co-branded credit card considerably more attractive.

Airline loyalty programmes and credit-card partnerships have become major businesses in their own right.

Southwest’s new lounges are explicitly tied to a new Chase credit card rather than a new business class cabin. The airline can sell the basic seat relatively cheaply, and customers willing to spend more can improve the journey with an upgraded airport wait.

Southwest’s latest announcement also shows how far low-cost segmentation can go. An airline built around a famously simple passenger proposition will soon have assigned seats, extra-legroom sections, multiple fare bundles and its own airport lounges.

title: Satreskrim Polsek Plaju Tangkap Terduga Pelaku Pembunuhan Nenek dalam Waktu 50 Menit
description:
Menerima laporan, Kapolsek Plaju AKP Sutioso, S.H., M.H., M.Si.
bersama Kanit Reskrim Polsek Plaju Ipda Feby Julian Pratama, S.H., M.M., beserta tim opsnal, pawas dan piket fungsi langsung mendatangi lokasi untuk melakukan olah tempat kejadian perkara.
Tim Unit Reskrim Polsek Plaju yang dipimpin langsung Kapolsek dan Kanit Reskrim kemudian bergerak menuju lokasi persembunyian pelaku.
Sonny Mahar Budi Adityawan, S.I.K., M.H.
Nandang Mu’min Wijaya, S.I.K., M.H.
text:
INDODAILY.CO, PALEMBANG, —- Polda Sumatera Selatan melalui jajaran Polrestabes Palembang bergerak cepat mengungkap kasus dugaan pembunuhan terhadap perempuan lanjut usia berinisial K (66) di Jalan Kapten Robani Kadir, Kelurahan Talang Putri, Kecamatan Plaju, Kota Palembang, Sabtu dini hari (12/9/2026).

Polisi menangkap AS (23), yang merupakan cucu kandung korban, sekitar 50 menit setelah peristiwa tersebut dilaporkan.

Peristiwa itu terungkap setelah warga sekitar mendengar teriakan korban meminta pertolongan sekitar pukul 00.45 WIB. Saksi kemudian menghubungi ketua RT dan keluarga korban sebelum bersama-sama mendatangi rumah korban.

Setelah berhasil masuk ke dalam rumah, saksi bersama anggota keluarga mendapati korban tergeletak di lantai dalam kondisi bersimbah darah. Warga kemudian melaporkan kejadian tersebut kepada pihak kepolisian.

Menerima laporan, Kapolsek Plaju AKP Sutioso, S.H., M.H., M.Si. bersama Kanit Reskrim Polsek Plaju Ipda Feby Julian Pratama, S.H., M.M., beserta tim opsnal, pawas dan piket fungsi langsung mendatangi lokasi untuk melakukan olah tempat kejadian perkara.

Petugas kemudian berkoordinasi dengan piket reskrim dan Unit Identifikasi Polrestabes Palembang. Korban selanjutnya dievakuasi ke Rumah Sakit Bhayangkara untuk menjalani pemeriksaan visum et repertum.

Dari informasi masyarakat, polisi memperoleh petunjuk mengenai keberadaan AS yang diduga melarikan diri setelah kejadian. Tim Unit Reskrim Polsek Plaju yang dipimpin langsung Kapolsek dan Kanit Reskrim kemudian bergerak menuju lokasi persembunyian pelaku.

Sekitar pukul 01.35 WIB, polisi berhasil menangkap AS tanpa perlawanan berarti. Petugas selanjutnya membawa AS ke Polsek Plaju untuk menjalani pemeriksaan dan proses hukum lebih lanjut.

Dalam pengungkapan tersebut, polisi turut mengamankan sejumlah barang bukti, yakni satu pisau bergagang kayu berwarna cokelat dengan ukuran kurang lebih 10 sentimeter, satu pisau bergagang warna putih-hitam dengan ukuran kurang lebih 10 sentimeter, serta satu gunting berwarna oranye.

Berdasarkan hasil pemeriksaan awal, korban mengalami luka pada bagian hidung, luka tusuk pada tangan kiri, serta luka lebam pada bagian wajah. Penyidik masih melakukan pendalaman terhadap rangkaian peristiwa tersebut.

Atas dugaan perbuatannya, AS dijerat Pasal 458 Kitab Undang-Undang Hukum Pidana (KUHP) terkait tindak pidana pembunuhan. Proses penyidikan terus dilakukan untuk memastikan seluruh fakta dan rangkaian kejadian terungkap secara terang.

Kapolrestabes Palembang Kombes Pol. Sonny Mahar Budi Adityawan, S.I.K., M.H. mengapresiasi respons cepat personel di lapangan serta peran masyarakat dalam memberikan informasi kepada kepolisian.

“Kami mengapresiasi kecepatan respons anggota di lapangan serta partisipasi aktif masyarakat sehingga pelaku dapat diamankan dalam waktu singkat, dan kami pastikan proses hukum berjalan tuntas untuk memberikan rasa keadilan,” ujar Sonny.

Kabid Humas Polda Sumatera Selatan Kombes Pol. Nandang Mu’min Wijaya, S.I.K., M.H. menegaskan bahwa kepolisian akan terus mengambil tindakan tegas terhadap setiap tindak pidana yang mengancam keselamatan masyarakat.

“Kami akan menindak tegas setiap bentuk kejahatan yang mengancam keselamatan jiwa masyarakat. Kami juga mengimbau seluruh warga untuk meningkatkan kepedulian terhadap lingkungan dan bersama-sama menjaga kamtibmas,” ujar Nandang.

BRICS countries on Saturday reaffirmed their commitment to deepen cooperation in the areas of policy, investment, technological and capacity building to develop sustainable transport infrastructure as well as promote use of sustainable aviation fuel to reduce carbon emissions.

At the meeting of the BRICS countries, chaired by India, the leaders also acknowledged the importance of embedding circular economy principles into the development and maintenance of transport infrastructure.

Advt

The BRICS meeting, which comprises 11 countries, is taking place in the national capital on September 12 and 13.

According to the New Delhi Declaration Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability, BRICS countries also acknowledged the importance of promoting Sustainable Aviation Fuels and low-carbon aviation fuels as means for reducing carbon emissions in international aviation.

"We reaffirm the commitment of BRICS countries to deepen cooperation in the areas of transport policy, investment, technological and capacity building with a view to develop sustainable and resilient transport infrastructure, recognising its critical role in economic growth, connectivity, and environmental sustainability," the declaration said.

They welcomed the BRICS Forum on Sustainable Aviation Fuels, the BRICS Framework of Cooperation for Exchange of Knowledge on Transport Decarbonisation while leveraging renewable energy potential.

BRICS Urban Mobility Hub for knowledge exchange and cooperation in accessible, affordable, inclusive, and smart urban transport solutions has also been set up.

"We welcome the establishment of the BRICS Logistics Supply-Chain Cooperation Framework and encourage discussion on the BRICS Railway Research Network proposal," the declaration said.

Further, the declaration said the countries will look forward to further promoting transport dialogue, including in civil aviation, to meet the demand of all stakeholders and to enhance the member countries' transport potential.

Advt

Transport cooperation will be carried out while respecting the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all member states, according to the declaration.

Also, the countries welcomed the expansion of the membership of the ICAO Council by adding four seats to underrepresented regions, including Africa and Asia Pacific.

The declaration said the members also welcomed the candidatures of Ethiopia, endorsed by the African Union as the sole African candidate, and Indonesia to assume the additional seats in the Council in the upcoming elections taking place during the 43rd (Extraordinary) ICAO Assembly.

text:
New Delhi: India supplied 895 crore litres of ethanol by the end of August under the Ethanol Supply Year (ESY) 2025-26 with grain-based feedstocks accounting for nearly 70 per cent of these cumulative supplies, according to data released by the All India Distillers’ Association (AIDA) on September.

According to the data, it is equivalent to around 85 per cent of the 1,048 crore litres contracted for the period.

According to AIDA, grain-based feedstocks contributed 624 crore litres of the total ethanol supplied, while sugar-based feedstocks accounted for 271 crore litres.

Among grain-based sources, maize was the largest contributor with 345 crore litres of ethanol supply. Surplus rice sourced from the Food Corporation of India (FCI) contributed 214 crore litres, while damaged food grains accounted for 64 crore litres.

Within the sugar-based segment, sugarcane juice contributed 149 crore litres by the end of August. B-heavy molasses supplied 107 crore litres and C-heavy molasses contributed 15 crore litres.

AIDA said the figures reflect the increasing diversification of India’s ethanol supply ecosystem, reducing dependence on any single feedstock pathway.

Commenting on the data, Bharati Balaji, Deputy Director General, AIDA, said nearly 70 per cent of the 895 crore litres supplied so far has come from grain-based feedstocks, led by maize and surplus FCI rice, while sugar-based sources continue to provide a significant share.

She said the diversity of feedstocks strengthens India’s ethanol programme by allowing the industry to utilise multiple domestic agricultural resources.

The association, however, noted that as domestic ethanol production capacity and supplies continue to expand, ensuring adequate and predictable demand avenues will become increasingly important.

According to AIDA, the issue will gain significance as India seeks to move beyond the current ethanol-blending programme and expand ethanol utilisation in flex-fuel vehicles (FFVs), compressed biogas (CBG), sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and other applications.

title: What is SAF and why does it matter to aviation? - Aerospace Global News
description:

text:
If aviation is going to cut its carbon emissions, it needs a way to keep aircraft flying without relying so heavily on fossil fuels. Sustainable aviation fuel, or SAF, is offering an interesting solution.

SAF is basically a jet fuel that can be made from renewable or waste materials instead of crude oil. And what’s great is that it can already be used in aircraft currently flying.

That makes SAF one of the most practical tools the aviation industry has for reducing its emissions in the short term. But there are still some big questions around how much can be produced, what it will cost and where the raw materials will come from.

What is sustainable aviation fuel?

SAF is a broad term for jet fuel made from non-fossil sources. Depending on the production method, those sources can include used cooking oil, animal fats, agricultural waste and other forms of biomass.

There are also newer technologies that can produce synthetic aviation fuel using renewable electricity, hydrogen and captured carbon dioxide.

SAF still produces CO₂ when it is burned in an aircraft engine. The difference is that the carbon used to make the fuel can come from sources that are already part of the carbon cycle, rather than from fossil carbon extracted from underground.

That can significantly reduce emissions across the fuel’s lifecycle, although the exact savings depend on how the SAF is produced.

How is SAF made?

There is no single recipe for making SAF. However, one of the most established methods uses waste oils and fats, which are processed into a fuel that has similar properties to conventional jet fuel.

Other production methods use biomass, waste materials or alcohols as their starting point.

Another area attracting attention is synthetic fuel, sometimes called e-SAF or power-to-liquid fuel. This approach can combine renewable hydrogen with carbon captured from the atmosphere or industrial processes.

The technology matters because not all SAF has the same environmental footprint. The source of the feedstock, the energy used during production and the way the fuel is transported all affect its overall emissions.

How are airlines using SAF at the moment?

SAF is designed to work with today’s aircraft and engines, so airlines don’t need to replace their fleets. It can also use much of the existing airport fuel infrastructure.

At present, SAF is generally blended with conventional jet fuel before being supplied to aircraft. The aviation industry is also working towards the wider use of fuels that can eventually be used without blending.

Airlines are already operating commercial passenger aircraft using SAF, so this is not simply a technology waiting in a laboratory. The challenge is making it available on a much larger scale.

Why does SAF matter to aviation?

Some parts of aviation are particularly difficult to decarbonise. For example, a long-haul aircraft needs to carry a huge amount of energy without adding excessive weight.

Current battery technology is not practical for most long-distance commercial aircraft, while hydrogen would require major changes to aircraft design and airport infrastructure. But SAF can fit into the system that already exists.

That does not mean it is the industry’s only answer. More efficient aircraft, improved operations, new propulsion technologies and better air traffic management will all still contribute to cutting emissions. SAF is simply one of the options that can make a difference right now.

What is holding SAF back?

The biggest problem is supply. Global SAF production remains tiny compared with the amount of conventional jet fuel used by the world’s airlines. Scaling up will require billions of dollars of investment, new production facilities and dependable supplies of suitable feedstocks.

Then there is the price. SAF generally costs more than conventional jet fuel, with the UK Ministry of Defence estimating conventional aviation fuel costing about $0.48 per litre, compared with $1.50 per litre for SAF. This is a massive challenge for airlines already operating in a highly competitive industry.

Governments are therefore playing an important role through mandates, incentives and other policies designed to encourage production and investment. In Europe, for example, the EU’s ReFuelEU Aviation rules require fuel suppliers to gradually increase the amount of SAF supplied at EU airports, starting at 2% in 2025 and rising to 70% by 2050. It’s a massive area of R&D.

What is the future of SAF?

SAF is not going to make aviation carbon-free. It is also unfortunately not a single solution to the industry’s climate challenge.

But it does offer a way to start cutting the carbon intensity of aviation without waiting for a completely new generation of aircraft. This is something few other technologies can provide.

The next step is to get it scaled up. If producers, airlines and governments can build a reliable supply of SAF while keeping its lifecycle emissions genuinely low, it could become a major part of aviation’s future.

Aviation cannot wait decades for the next generation of aircraft to solve its emissions problem. SAF gives the industry a way to start cutting carbon today, using the aircraft it already has. That makes it a very important area for growth and development.

text:
New Delhi: An Air India pilot died in Delhi while on a scheduled layover, shortly before he was due to operate his next flight. The incident occurred at a hotel in Vasant Kunj on September 11, 2026, and Delhi Police has begun an investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death.

The pilot was identified in media reports as Captain Sunny Asladekar, who was in his 40s. He had reportedly been staying at The Grand hotel in Vasant Kunj as part of his operational and training schedule.

Pilot Found Unresponsive During Delhi Layover

According to reports, Captain Asladekar had checked into the hotel on September 10. He was subsequently found unconscious inside his room on the evening of September 11.

Concern arose after his brother was unable to contact him. Hotel staff were alerted and found the room locked from inside. The door was opened using a master key, after which the pilot was found unresponsive.

He was immediately taken to a hospital, where he was declared brought dead. Delhi Police was informed and initiated proceedings to establish the circumstances of the death.

Pilot Was Scheduled to Fly the Following Morning

The incident occurred during a scheduled rest period before the pilot’s next assignment. Reports indicate that he was scheduled to operate a flight early on Saturday morning.

The circumstances are significant from an aviation-operations perspective because airline pilots must meet strict medical fitness, fatigue-management and operational-readiness requirements before being assigned flight duties.

The pilot had previously been associated with Air India Express and had moved to Air India a few months earlier, according to reports.

Boeing 787 Conversion Training

Reports also indicate that Captain Asladekar was undergoing conversion training for the Boeing 787.

Transitioning between aircraft types is a structured process. Pilots require appropriate type-specific training and competency assessment before operating a different aircraft type. The Boeing 787 is a wide-body, long-haul aircraft with flight-deck systems, procedures and operating characteristics that require dedicated training.

For aviation students and AME professionals, this highlights an important principle of commercial aviation: aircraft-specific competency and crew fitness are essential components of flight safety.

What Is Known About the Cause of Death?

At this stage, the circumstances should not be confused with an established aviation accident or an aircraft-related technical event.

An airline statement reported that the pilot was found unconscious during his hotel layover and was taken to hospital, where he was declared dead. Some reports have cited cardiac arrest as the suspected or reported medical cause. However, Delhi Police has continued its investigation and the post-mortem process is important in establishing the official cause of death.

Therefore, any definitive conclusion about the cause of death should await the appropriate medical and investigative findings.

Delhi Police Investigation Underway

Delhi Police has examined the circumstances at the hotel and initiated the necessary legal proceedings. A crime team reportedly inspected the scene, while a post-mortem examination was conducted at Safdarjung Hospital.

Investigators are expected to establish the sequence of events, examine available evidence and await medical findings before determining the circumstances surrounding the death.

Aviation Safety Significance

Although the incident did not involve an aircraft in flight, it highlights an important aspect of aviation safety: pilot fitness is a critical part of the overall safety system.

Airline operations depend not only on aircraft serviceability and maintenance but also on the physical and mental fitness of flight crew. Airlines therefore operate within regulatory frameworks covering areas such as:

Pilot medical fitness

Fatigue risk management

Rest and duty-time requirements

Pre-flight fitness assessment

Crew scheduling

Training and competency checks

Operational readiness

For Aircraft Maintenance Engineers (AMEs) and aviation students, the incident is a reminder that aviation safety is a multidisciplinary system. Aircraft maintenance, engineering controls, flight operations, crew training, medical fitness and regulatory oversight all contribute to safe operations.

Air India’s Response

Air India expressed sadness over the death of its cockpit crew member and said it was in contact with the pilot’s family and providing support during the difficult period.

The airline’s operational arrangements would also need to ensure that flight duties are assigned only to appropriately qualified and medically fit crew members.

Conclusion

The death of an Air India pilot during a Delhi layover, shortly before his scheduled flight, has prompted a police investigation and medical examination. While reports have pointed toward a medical emergency, the official findings will be important before a definitive cause can be established.

Es ist demnach „ein strukturiertes wissenschaftliches Dokument, das den Ablauf, die Ergebnisse und die Schlussfolgerung eines praktischen Experiments oder einer Untersuchung beschreibt“.
Power-to-X, kurz PtX, ist einerseits Chemie, die in der Praxis allerdings an der Physik und der Ökonomie scheitert, weshalb die Branche bittere Tränen weint und dringend nach einer Erzählung sucht, die ihre Geschäftsidee stabilisieren könnte.
Häufig ist die Klimatisierung solcher Systeme nur unzureichend auf Hitze ausgelegt, gerade bei älteren Fahrzeugen“.
text:
Ich muss im Moment ganz schön Gas geben, um dem Paradigmenwechsel auf den Fersen zu bleiben. Das herrschende Paradigma wechselt gerade so rasant die Spur wie Max Verstappen, der aus dem Windschatten heraus einen Ferrari überholt. Laut Lexikon ist ein Paradigma „ein grundlegendes Denkmuster, Weltbild oder Vorbild, das als verbindlicher Rahmen für das Denken, Handeln oder die wissenschaftliche Arbeit in einer bestimmten Zeit dient“. Und wenn dieses wechselt, sollte man nicht zu spät kommen. Ein einfaches Beispiel: Der Übergang vom geozentrischen Weltbild („die Sonne kreist um die Erde“) zum heliozentrischen Weltbild („die Erde kreist um die Sonne“) war ein solcher Paradigmenwechsel. Und die katholische Kirche hat‘s vermasselt. Eine ewige Warnung an die Glaubensfesten jeglicher Couleur.

Die Anhänger des CO2-zentrierten Weltbildes haben daraus gelernt und sind derzeit so wachsam wie eine Löwenmutter, die spürt, wie die Hyänen um sie herumkreisen. Denn was gestern noch mit der Rettung des Weltklimas begründet wurde, wird heute mit der Kriegstüchtigkeit gerechtfertigt. Ein echter Paradigmenwechsel, bei dem lediglich das Förderziel das gleiche bleibt. Und so flatterte aus dem fernen Cottbus an der Lausitz ein sogenanntes „Lab Paper“ auf meinen Schreibtisch, das den schönen Titel trägt: „Vom fossilen Risiko zur synthetischen Resilienz – PtX-Kraftstoffe im Militär“. Und gleich im ersten Satz heißt es:

„Der Klimawandel und seine Folgen sind eine zentrale Herausforderung für heutige Streitkräfte. Während als Antwort auf den russischen Angriffskrieg gegen die Ukraine eine Neuausrichtung der NATO-Streitkräfte auf die Landes- und Bündnisverteidigung stattfindet, darf die Anpassung an den Klimawandel nicht vernachlässigt werden. Nur wenn das Militär zugleich nachhaltiger und klimaresilienter wird, kann es auch künftig seine Einsatz- und Verteidigungsfähigkeit sichern“.

Das Wort „Lab Paper“ steht dabei nicht für – wie der Unbedarfte jetzt meinen könnte – „Laberpapier“, sondern entstammt dem in gebildeten Kreisen gebräuchlichen Neudeutschen. Es ist demnach „ein strukturiertes wissenschaftliches Dokument, das den Ablauf, die Ergebnisse und die Schlussfolgerung eines praktischen Experiments oder einer Untersuchung beschreibt“. Kurzum: Ein Lab Paper ist stets schwer intelligent. Das vorliegende ist, wie ich aus dem vorangegangenen Zitat messerscharf folgere, sogar zweifach intelligent, ein sogenannter „Doppelwumms“, um die einzige Formulierung zu gebrauchen, die von Olaf Scholz in Erinnerung bleiben wird.

Den Kommissköpfen die Weltrettung plausibel machen

Das PtX Lab Lausitz gehört zur bundeseigenen, gemeinnützigen „Zukunft – Umwelt – Gesellschaft (ZUG gGmbH)“ und arbeitet im Auftrag des Bundesministeriums für Wirtschaft und Energie. Zu seinen Aufgaben gehört der sogenannte „Markthochlauf von PtX-Produkten“. Power-to-X, kurz PtX, ist einerseits Chemie, die in der Praxis allerdings an der Physik und der Ökonomie scheitert, weshalb die Branche bittere Tränen weint und dringend nach einer Erzählung sucht, die ihre Geschäftsidee stabilisieren könnte. Die Idee: Man nehme elektrischen Strom, stelle mit dessen Hilfe aus Wasser oder auch Erdgas Wasserstoff her und synthetisiere daraus anschließend einen transportablen (Kohlenwasserstoff-) Sprit. Das Problem: Jede dieser Umwandlungen verursacht Verluste, hinzu kommen Anlagen-, CO2-Bereitstellungs- und Transportkosten. Das stellt das Lab Paper auch gar nicht in Abrede: „Es entsteht ein selbstverstärkender Kreislauf aus geringer Nachfrage, begrenztem Angebot und hohen Preisen, der zu niedrigen Marktvolumina führt und den weiteren Markthochlauf mittelfristig hemmt“. Und – was nicht da steht: langfristig in die Pleite führt.

Aber, um mit Dieter Bohlen zu sprechen: „Erklär mal einem Bekloppten, dass der bekloppt ist“. Also warum einfach, wenn es auch kompliziert geht? Das Verfahren ist ungefähr so, als würde die Feldküche der Gebirgsschützen in Garmisch die Kartoffeln nicht mehr einfach beim Lidl kaufen, sondern zunächst in Stärke, Wasser und Mineralstoffe zerlegen, um daraus anschließend wieder Kartoffeln zusammenzubauen. Der entscheidende Unterschied: Bei Kartoffeln würde vermutlich jemand fragen, was der Unsinn kostet. E-Fuels sind bis zu zehnmal teurer als herkömmliche Kraftstoffe, die ja auch kein Sonderangebot sind. Sagt sogar die Bundeswehr.

Um den Kommissköpfen die Weltrettung dennoch plausibel zu machen, muss man schon zu den für die Broschüre zuständigen „Mitarbeitenden“ des PTX Lab Lausitz gehören und Völkerrecht oder Public Policy and Human Development studiert haben. Dann aber klappt es prima.

Und damit komme ich zum entscheidenden Satz des gesamten Lab-Papers: Militärische Abnehmer, heißt es dort, wiesen eine „geringere Preissensitivität“ auf, weil „Wirtschaftlichkeit kein hervorgehobener Entscheidungsparameter ist“. Deshalb könnten die Streitkräfte auch bei höheren Marktpreisen langfristige Abnahmemengen garantieren. Endlich ein Kunde, der nicht so genau auf den Preis schaut! Das Sondervermögen bei der Arbeit.

Man trifft zwei Fliegen mit einer Kanone

Das Bestechende dabei ist nämlich: Man trifft zwei Fliegen mit einer Kanone. Die Verfasser haben ein Problem erkannt, das Panzerkommandanten an der ukrainischen Front oder F35-Piloten am Golf bislang irgendwie entgangen ist: Der Krieg muss nicht nur gewonnen, sondern auch „defossilisiert“ werden. Die laufende Modernisierung der NATO berge die Gefahr eines „fossilen Lock-in“. Nur wenn das Militär zugleich „nachhaltiger und klimaresilienter“ werde, könne es auch künftig seine Einsatz- und Verteidigungsfähigkeit sichern – und die Zuschüsse für den Hochlauf von PtX.

Früher musste PtX das Klima retten. Jetzt schützt PtX auch noch vor dem Russ, dem Ami und demnächst wohl auch dem Franzos, wenn Le Pens Rassemblement National im Frühjahr die Wahl gewinnt. PtX ist deshalb nicht mehr teuer, sondern resilient. Und es schlägt die Stunde der Lyriker: Staatliche Nachfrage bedeutet nicht Subvention, sondern strategische Autonomie.

Während man bislang glaubte, ein Soldat im Schützenpanzer müsse sich hauptsächlich vor Artillerie, Minen, Panzerfäusten und Drohnen fürchten, entdeckt PtX Lab weitere furchtbare Feinde: Der steigende Meeresspiegel verursacht bei der Einsatzflotille 2 in Wilhelmshaven nasse Socken (sofern es gerade welche gibt); Desertifikation wirbelt den Sand auf dem Truppenübungsplatz Grafenwöhr auf und vernebelt dem Hubschrauber die Sicht; höhere Temperaturen machen die Luft dünner und der Eurofighter kriegt am Fliegerhorst Landsberg den Hintern nicht mehr hoch. „Darüber hinaus sind auch die Soldatinnen und Soldaten selbst gesteigerten Risiken ausgesetzt“, schreiben die um das Wohl der Truppe Besorgten:

„Hitzeschäden treten während Einsätzen und Übungen häufiger auf, während Extremwetterereignisse eine zusätzliche Umweltbedrohung darstellen. Die doktringemäße Nutzung von Fahrzeugen und Ausrüstung – also deren Einsatz entsprechend den in Vorschriften und Plänen zugrunde gelegten Annahmen – ist in Teilen nicht mehr umsetzbar. Bereits bei Außentemperaturen um 35 °C können in gepanzerten Fahrzeugen extreme Innenraumtemperaturen entstehen. Häufig ist die Klimatisierung solcher Systeme nur unzureichend auf Hitze ausgelegt, gerade bei älteren Fahrzeugen“.

Der deutsche Frontsoldat ist mithin Risiken ausgesetzt, die normalerweise nur dem Bahnkunden drohen, der mit dem ICE 512 bei ausgefallener Klimaanlage Richtung Berlin unterwegs ist, um Tante Käthe zu besuchen.

„Verteidige Freiheit, Demokratie und die Beimischungsquote für Sustainable Aviation Fuel“

Es muss also dringend etwas geschehen. Zumal auch der Ruf der Truppe ohne PtX gefährdet ist. „Die Defossilisierung des Militärs erhöht zudem dessen Legitimation“, schreiben die Autoren. Hohe Emissionen könnten das Vertrauen in der Bevölkerung beschädigen und womöglich sogar die Personalgewinnung erschweren. Das eröffnet ungeahnte Möglichkeiten für die Nachwuchswerbung: „Mach, was wirklich zählt. Verteidige Freiheit, Demokratie und die Beimischungsquote für Sustainable Aviation Fuel.“ Es hilft also alles nix: „Die Streitkräfte müssen – wie jeder andere Sektor auch – ihren Beitrag zur Erreichung von Klimaneutralität leisten“.

Und dann kommt das schwere Geschütz Kaliber 155:

„Gleichzeitig bietet die Verfehlung dieses Ziels einen Anknüpfungspunkt für Desinformationskampagnen als Teil hybrider Kriegsführung sowie für die Instrumentalisierung durch extremistische Akteure.“

Gefahr ist im Verzug:

„Argumentationsmuster, die staatliche Klimapolitik als unzureichend darstellen und daraus eine Legitimation für Widerstand gegen staatliche Ordnung ableiten, finden sich in Teilen linksextremistischer und islamistischer Ideologien“.

Ja, und in den Parteiprogrammen von CDU, SPD, Linken, Grünen und in einem Urteil des Bundes-Verfassungsgerichtes.

Die Lage ist wirklich ernst. Wie hieß es bei der Bundeswehr zum Einsatz in Mali: „Licht aus. Energie und Wasser sparen kann jeder, auch im Einsatz.“ Die Truppenküche biete täglich vegetarische Gerichte an, auch vegane Mahlzeiten lassen sich aus den Komponenten zusammenstellen, und der Anteil der Bio-Lebensmittel werde „stetig steigend“ berücksichtigt. Selbst die Einpersonenpackung ist inzwischen mit Chili sin carne vorbereitet. Das neue Ideal deutscher Kriegstüchtigkeit lässt sich somit auf die Formel bringen: „Zäh wie Mehrwegplastik, hart wie grüner Stahl und flink wie Öko-Opportunisten“.

Im Achgut-Buchshop erhältlich:

„Hilfe, mein Hund überholt mich rechts! – Geständnisse eines Sonntagsfahrers“ von Dirk Maxeiner, Achgut Edition 2018, hier bestellbar.

text:
Jakarta: PT Pertamina Hulu Energi (PHE) kembali menorehkan prestasi dalam penguatan tata kelola perusahaan dengan meraih empat penghargaan pada ajang TOP Government, Risk & Compliance (GRC) Awards 2026 yang mengusung tema “Sustainability by Design: A Journey Through Intelligent GRC”.

Empat penghargaan yang berhasil diraih PHE meliputi TOP GRC Awards 2026 #5 Star, The High Performing Board of Commissioner on GRC 2026, The Most Committed GRC Leader 2026, serta TOP GRC Awards 2026 – Special Appreciation for Risk Culture and Maturity.

Pencapaian tersebut menjadi apresiasi atas konsistensi PHE dalam memperkuat penerapan Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) sebagai bagian integral dari pengelolaan bisnis perusahaan. Implementasi GRC tidak hanya diarahkan untuk memastikan kepatuhan terhadap ketentuan dan standar yang berlaku, tetapi juga menjadi bagian penting dalam mendukung pengambilan keputusan bisnis yang prudent, adaptif, dan berkelanjutan.

Direktur Manajemen Risiko PT Pertamina Hulu Energi, Whisnu Bahriansyah menyampaikan, penerapan GRC di PHE selaras dengan visi dan misi perusahaan dalam menjaga ketahanan energi nasional sekaligus bertransformasi menjadi perusahaan hulu migas kelas dunia yang andal dan berkelanjutan.

“Dengan bisnis hulu migas yang memiliki tingkat risiko tinggi, penerapan intelligent GRC kami mulai dari tahap perencanaan, pengambilan keputusan, eksekusi, hingga monitoring dan evaluasi. Aspek governance, risk, dan compliance dirancang agar manajemen mampu mengambil keputusan secara lebih cepat, tepat, dan tetap berada dalam koridor tata kelola perusahaan,” katanya dalam keterangan tertulisnya, Minggu, 13 September 2026.

(Ilustrasi. Foto: Dok PHE)

Hasil kolaborasi berbagai pihak

Lebih lanjut, Whisnu menegaskan bahwa keberhasilan penerapan GRC merupakan hasil kolaborasi seluruh elemen perusahaan. Menurutnya, penguatan tata kelola, manajemen risiko, kepatuhan, serta budaya sadar risiko membutuhkan keterlibatan aktif dari seluruh insan PHE.

“Terima kasih kepada seluruh karyawan, khususnya tim Governance, Risk Management, Compliance, Internal Audit, dan seluruh unit kerja. Apresiasi juga kami sampaikan kepada regulator, mitra bisnis, pelanggan, dan seluruh pemangku kepentingan atas kepercayaan dan dukungannya,” tutur Whisnu.

Perolehan empat penghargaan pada TOP GRC Awards 2026 ini menjadi motivasi untuk terus memperkuat tata kelola, budaya sadar risiko, dan kepatuhan perusahaan.

text:
Rantai Pasok Global dan Bioekonomi: Memanfaatkan Potensi Keanekaragaman Hayati Sebagai Mesin Baru Perekonomian Nasional

Analisis Komprehensif Transformasi Ekonomi Hijau Berbasis Keanekaragaman Hayati Indonesia

1. Pendahuluan: Wajah Baru Perekonomian Global

Dinamika perekonomian global dalam satu dekade terakhir mengalami pergeseran fundamental. Krisis iklim, disrupsi rantai pasok (supply chain) internasional akibat ketegangan geopolitik, serta kesadaran kolektif akan pentingnya pembangunan berkelanjutan telah mendorong perombakan besar-besaran pada model pertumbuhan ekonomi konvensional. Model ekstraktif yang bertumpu pada eksploitasi sumber daya fosil dan bahan mentah tanpa batas kian ditinggalkan. Di tengah lanskap global yang kompetitif dan rentan ini, konsep bioekonomi (bioeconomy) muncul sebagai mercusuar baru, menawarkan sintesis antara pertumbuhan ekonomi berdaya saing tinggi dan pelestarian lingkungan hidup.

Bagi Indonesia, sebuah negara kepulauan megabiodiversitas terbesar kedua di dunia, transisi menuju bioekonomi bukan lagi sekadar pilihan alternatif, melainkan sebuah keharusan strategis (strategic imperative). Dengan kekayaan flora, fauna, dan ekosistem laut yang tak ternilai harganya, Indonesia memiliki modal fundamental untuk memimpin rantai pasok global produk-produk berbasis biologis (bio-based products). Artikel ini mengkaji bagaimana integrasi antara pengelolaan rantai pasok global dan potensi keanekaragaman hayati dapat menjadi mesin baru penggerak perekonomian nasional yang inklusif, resilien, dan berkelanjutan.

2. Memahami Bioekonomi dan Integrasinya dengan Rantai Pasok Global

Secara konseptual, bioekonomi mencakup seluruh kegiatan ekonomi yang melibatkan penggunaan sumber daya hayati terbarukan dari darat dan laut---seperti tanaman, hutan, hewan, mikroorganisme, dan biomassa limbah---untuk memproduksi pangan, pakan, energi bio, serta produk bernilai tambah tinggi di sektor kimia, farmasi, kosmetik, dan material maju.

Dalam konteks rantai pasok global modern, terjadi pergeseran permintaan dari konsumen internasional. Pasar global saat ini semakin menuntut ketertelusuran (traceability), transparansi, dan keberlanjutan (sustainability) dari hulu hingga hilir. Integrasi bioekonomi ke dalam rantai pasok global menuntut industri nasional untuk bertransformasi melalui beberapa pilar utama:

* Ketertelusuran Rantai Pasok (Supply Chain Traceability): Memastikan bahwa komoditas bio-based yang diekspor berasal dari sumber yang legal, tidak merusak hutan (deforestation-free), dan menghormati hak-hak masyarakat lokal.

* Ekonomi Sirkular (Circular Bioeconomy): Memanfaatkan limbah industri pertanian, perkebunan, dan kehutanan (seperti cangkang sawit, sekam padi, bagas tebu, dan limbah pengolahan ikan) sebagai bahan baku bernilai tambah tinggi untuk bio-energi dan bioplastik.

* Standarisasi dan Sertifikasi Internasional: Memenuhi standar kualitas global yang ketat, termasuk sertifikasi organik, ekolabel, serta kepatuhan terhadap regulasi lingkungan internasional seperti EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR).

3. Potensi Strategis Keanekaragaman Hayati Indonesia

Indonesia dianugerahi kekayaan keanekaragaman hayati yang menempatkannya pada posisi strategis global. Hutan hujan tropis yang luas, terumbu karang terkaya di dunia dalam Segitiga Terumbu Karang (Coral Triangle), serta ribuan pulau dengan ekosistem unik menyimpan potensi raksasa yang belum tergarap secara optimal.

Tabel berikut merangkum sektor-sektor kunci keanekaragaman hayati Indonesia dan kontribusinya dalam rantai pasok global:

Sektor Bioekonomi

Farmasi & Kosmetik Alami

Bahan baku industri obat herbal global, kosmetik organik, dan aromaterapi premium.

Selulosa kayu, rumput laut, pati singkong dan sagu

text:
New Delhi: India supplied 895 crore litres of ethanol by the end of August under the Ethanol Supply Year (ESY) 2025-26 with grain-based feedstocks accounting for nearly 70 per cent of these cumulative supplies, according to data released by the All India Distillers' Association (AIDA) on Saturday.

According to the data, it is equivalent to around 85 per cent of the 1,048 crore litres contracted for the period.

According to AIDA, grain-based feedstocks contributed 624 crore litres of the total ethanol supplied, while sugar-based feedstocks accounted for 271 crore litres.

Among grain-based sources, maize was the largest contributor with 345 crore litres of ethanol supply. Surplus rice sourced from the Food Corporation of India (FCI) contributed 214 crore litres, while damaged food grains accounted for 64 crore litres.

Within the sugar-based segment, sugarcane juice contributed 149 crore litres by the end of August. B-heavy molasses supplied 107 crore litres and C-heavy molasses contributed 15 crore litres.

AIDA said the figures reflect the increasing diversification of India's ethanol supply ecosystem, reducing dependence on any single feedstock pathway.

Commenting on the data, Bharati Balaji, Deputy Director General, AIDA, said nearly 70 per cent of the 895 crore litres supplied so far has come from grain-based feedstocks, led by maize and surplus FCI rice, while sugar-based sources continue to provide a significant share.

She said the diversity of feedstocks strengthens India's ethanol programme by allowing the industry to utilise multiple domestic agricultural resources.

The association, however, noted that as domestic ethanol production capacity and supplies continue to expand, ensuring adequate and predictable demand avenues will become increasingly important.

According to AIDA, the issue will gain significance as India seeks to move beyond the current ethanol-blending programme and expand ethanol utilisation in flex-fuel vehicles (FFVs), compressed biogas (CBG), sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and other applications.

title: Jackdaw: UK nears approval of the deposit - Inspenet
description:
The UK government is nearing a new decision on Jackdaw, the North Sea natural gas project that has been at the center of an energy and environmental dispute for years.
Increased gas production within British waters would add a domestic source to the system.
Although both projects are often mentioned together in the North Sea debate, their processes are being studied separately.
Jackdaw tests the UK's energy future Ultimately, the decision regarding Jackdaw will have a significance that goes beyond a single site.
If it receives final approval, the UK will add new domestic natural gas production in a relatively short time.
text:
The UK government is nearing a new decision on Jackdaw, the North Sea natural gas project that has been at the center of an energy and environmental dispute for years. Authorization could come in September and would pave the way for production to begin in the following months.

The potential breakthrough comes as the UK seeks to bolster its energy security and reduce its reliance on imports. At the same time, the government must balance this strategy with its climate commitments and the opposition from various environmental groups.

Jackdaw is particularly significant because much of the necessary infrastructure is already in place. Therefore, authorization would allow the integration of new British gas production in a much shorter timeframe than is typical for an energy project of this scale.

Jackdaw could begin supplying gas this winter

The project is in a very advanced stage, Shell and Equinor operate Jackdaw through Adura and assure that the necessary infrastructure is 99% complete.

This means that natural gas could begin flowing during the coming winter if the authorities complete the authorization process on time.

In this way, Jackdaw presents a significant difference compared to projects that still require years of construction. Much of the investment and physical work has already been completed, so the regulatory decision has become one of the last obstacles to commencing operations.

However, the approval is not yet finalized; Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh must issue her recommendation, and subsequently the North Sea Transition Authority must complete the corresponding process.

How much gas can Jackdaw supply to the UK?

On the other hand, the volume that the project could bring is one of the main arguments of its operators.

According to estimates presented by the responsible companies, Jackdaw would have the capacity to represent around 6% of British gas production during its peak activity period.

That percentage is significant in a country that relies on foreign supplies to meet some of its energy needs. Increased gas production within British waters would add a domestic source to the system.

However, the impact on the market must be analyzed with caution; production from a single deposit does not eliminate dependence on imports nor does it guarantee a reduction in the prices paid by households and businesses.

Furthermore, the North Sea industry is in a mature stage; much of its commercially attractive reserves have already been exploited, and this limits the scope for recovering production levels recorded decades ago.

Energy security returns to the center of the British debate

The government led by Andy Burnham has taken a pragmatic stance on oil and gas. The Prime Minister has acknowledged that these sources will remain part of the energy system for an extended period while the transition to other technologies progresses.

This proposal places the North Sea back at the heart of the energy security debate. The issue is no longer solely about how much fuel remains available; it also addresses how much the UK should produce domestically versus how much it is willing to import.

The government also believes that the sector remains linked to jobs and economic activity in areas that have been tied to hydrocarbon extraction for decades. The impact of the energy transition on workers in northeast Scotland is also part of this debate.

Why was Jackdaw's previous authorization revoked?

However, Jackdaw had already completed a significant part of the administrative process.

The project obtained permits years ago, along with other North Sea projects. Subsequently, environmental groups took the case to court and challenged how its climate impacts had been assessed.

A judge ruled that the assessments must take into account the emissions generated when the extracted oil and gas are ultimately used. As a result, the previous environmental permits for Jackdaw and Rosebank were invalidated.

The companies then had to resubmit the necessary environmental documentation.

For this reason, the current process is not simply about granting a new exploration license. Jackdaw already has a license, and the outstanding issue is the environmental permits required to develop the operation under the criteria established after the court decision.

Shell and Equinor have the project practically finished.

Likewise, the state of the facilities explains why a government decision could have consequences in a relatively short period.

Shell and Equinor have invested heavily in the development of Jackdaw and now jointly operate their British assets through Adura. The infrastructure built brings the project close to the stage where gas can be brought to market.

For companies, starting production would allow them to capitalize on an investment that is already well underway. For the UK, it would mean adding to domestic supply during a period marked by increased attention to energy costs and fuel availability.

The situation also highlights the regulatory risks associated with large hydrocarbon projects. Even an operation with nearly completed infrastructure can be halted when its permits are challenged in court.

The Rosebank site will be the next big decision

Meanwhile, the Rosebank field is keeping another far-reaching decision open for the British energy sector.

Although both projects are often mentioned together in the North Sea debate, their processes are being studied separately. Therefore, authorization for Jackdaw does not automatically imply that Rosebank will receive the same treatment.

Rosebank is also on a different scale; estimates place its resources at up to 500 million barrels of oil or its equivalent, making it the largest undeveloped deposit in British waters.

Authorities are still studying its environmental impact; a decision could come later, and the government is analyzing ways to allocate some of the revenue related to the project to clean energy investments.

Thus, the outcome of the Rosebank field will serve as another signal regarding the strategy that the United Kingdom intends to pursue with the remaining North Sea reserves.

Environmental groups maintain their opposition

On the other hand, any eventual authorization of Jackdaw will hardly put an end to the conflict.

Environmental groups argue that developing new oil fields prolongs dependence on fossil fuels and generates emissions incompatible with climate goals. These organizations also question whether the increase in domestic supply will directly translate into cheaper energy for consumers.

The opposition has already had concrete consequences; previous legal actions forced a review of the environmental assessments of Jackdaw and Rosebank and delayed the development of both projects.

Therefore, any new authorization will have to be based on an assessment capable of meeting the environmental requirements established by the courts. The government will have to justify how the project fits within its energy and climate strategy.

Jackdaw tests the UK's energy future

Ultimately, the decision regarding Jackdaw will have a significance that goes beyond a single site.

Its potential launch will show the extent to which the United Kingdom is willing to maintain North Sea gas production while increasing investments aimed at transforming its energy system.

The country faces two simultaneous pressures. It needs to ensure sufficient energy for homes and businesses while simultaneously seeking to reduce emissions over the coming decades.

Jackdaw sits squarely at the heart of this tension. If it receives final approval, the UK will add new domestic natural gas production in a relatively short time. However, the project will also keep alive the debate about how much oil and gas the country should continue to extract during its energy transition.

Next will come another, larger-scale test: the Rosebank field. Decisions on both projects will help define the role the North Sea will play in British energy policy for years to come.

News of additional interest

Milei intensifies pressure over Falklands oil

Argentine President Javier Milei escalated tensions over the Falkland Islands by warning that his government will impose sanctions on oil companies involved in projects in the area that lack Argentine authorization. The president reiterated Argentina's sovereignty claim and described the Sea Lion oil development, located approximately 220 kilometers north of the archipelago, as a "clear and imminent danger."

The warning specifically targets the project operated by Navitas Petroleum Development and Production and Rockhopper Exploration. Sea Lion has already reached its final investment decision, and its managers expect to begin oil extraction in March 2028. The development includes a first phase of 11 subsea wells and a second phase with another 12 wells. Production could be sustained for more than 30 years.

AI is changing the rules of the energy game

The energy industry is learning from the lessons of five years of transitioning to cleaner energy sources. During a panel at the AFPM Summit, experts suggested that new projects must respond to proven regional demand, manage capital wisely, and identify logistical problems from the outset. They also recommended evaluating suppliers, raw materials, and equipment in advance to avoid delays once investments have already been committed.

Now another pressure is emerging: the rapid growth of artificial intelligence and data centers. Electricity availability is already a key part of initial discussions with clients, while equipment such as transformers and compressors face supply constraints. Added to this is a shortage of skilled workers. The panel also highlighted that sustainable aviation fuel production remains below targets despite airline demand and refinery capacity.

Diesel breaks records and threatens wallets

The average price of diesel in the United States reached a record $5,820 per gallon amid increasingly tight global supply. Tensions with Iran and Ukraine's attacks on Russian refineries have reduced international supply. Russia even suspended its diesel exports until September 30. Since the end of February, the price of the fuel has risen by 55%.

The pressure comes as US fuel reserves are at very low levels. In August, distillate inventories reached their lowest average for that month since 1982. The situation is most critical on the East Coast, where stocks have fallen to 19.3 million barrels. Furthermore, autumn will bring increased consumption due to harvests and transportation, while winter will raise the demand for heating oil.

Arcadia and MB Energy are preparing the eSAF route

Arcadia eFuels and MB Energy have signed a memorandum of understanding to explore the development of a European synthetic aviation fuel (eSAF) supply chain. Arcadia will contribute its production expertise, while MB Energy will assess its role in fuel procurement and distribution. The goal is to connect production plants with airlines and other customers in the European market.

The collaboration will study the entire eSAF commercial lifecycle, from transport and storage to blending and final delivery. The companies aim to create a system capable of handling larger volumes as demand grows and European regulations to reduce aviation emissions become more stringent. The agreement will also allow them to explore how to leverage MB Energy's existing infrastructure and business relationships within the energy sector.
